# vite-plugin-seo-meta - Full Context

> Generated by docmd

---

## [API](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/api/) (API)

---
title: "API"
description: "Public exports: seo(), defineSeoConfig() and the runtime helper."
---

## `seo(options?)`

The Vite plugin. Returns a Vite `Plugin` (gasp, i know, how shocking).

```ts
import { seo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [seo({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site" } })],
});
```

### Options

| Option       | Type                                         | Default           | Notes                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `site`       | `SiteConfig`                                 | -                 | Site defaults                                          |
| `pages`      | `Record<string, PageMeta>`                   | `{}`              | Per-page overrides                                     |
| `robots`     | `"auto"` \| `boolean` \| `RobotsFileOptions` | `"auto"`          | `false` disables generation                            |
| `sitemap`    | `"auto"` \| `boolean` \| `SitemapOptions`    | `"auto"`          | `false` disables generation                            |
| `validate`   | `"warn"` \| `"error"` \| `false`             | `"warn"`          | Validation policy                                      |
| `configFile` | `string` \| `false`                          | `"seo.config.ts"` | Path to config file, or `false` to skip auto-detection |

## `defineSeoConfig(config)`

A typed identity function that returns its argument unchanged. This only exists so that the config can be easily typechecked.

```ts
import { defineSeoConfig } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta";

export default defineSeoConfig({
  site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site" },
  pages: { "/about": { title: "About" } },
});
```

The plugin auto-detects `seo.config.ts` in the project root and loads it. Set `configFile: false` to disable this.

## `applySeo(page, site?)`

Runtime helper for SPAs. Updates managed head elements after a route change.

```ts
import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime";

applySeo({ title: "New Page", description: "..." });
```

See [SPA Runtime](./spa-runtime.md). (No, no, not a spa, a Single-Page Application, though we _all_ would love that... probably.)

## Exported types

The plugin exports types for every config shape:

- `SeoPluginOptions` - options accepted by `seo()`
- `SeoOptions` - the full beeg config (site, pages, robots, sitemap, validate)
- `SiteConfig` - site defaults
- `PageMeta` - per-page overrides
- `OpenGraphInfo` - Open Graph values
- `TwitterInfo` - Twitter Card values
- `FaviconConfig` - favicon and platform icons
- `RobotsFileOptions` - robots.txt options
- `RobotsGroup` - an RFC 9309 agent group
- `SitemapOptions` - sitemap options
- `ImageRef` / `ImageInput` - image references, including `thumbnail` for video sitemaps
- `JsonLdConfig` - JSON-LD configuration
- `HreflangAlternate` - a hreflang entry
- `ThemeColorEntry` - a theme color meta tag
- `TwitterCardType` - `summary` \| `summary_large_image` \| `player` \| `app`
- `TwitterHandle` - a Twitter `@handle`
- `TwitterAppPlatform` - `iphone` \| `ipad` \| `googleplay`
- `TwitterPlayer` - player card iframe config
- `TwitterApps` - app card per-platform config
- `ArticleJsonLd` / `OrganizationJsonLd` / `WebSiteJsonLd` / `ProductJsonLd` / `JsonLdPerson` - JSON-LD shapes
- `OpenGraphArticle` / `OpenGraphBook` / `OpenGraphMusic` / `OpenGraphVideo` / `OpenGraphPayment` - Open Graph verticals
- `SitemapChangefreq` - changefreq enum
- `RobotsDirectives` - structured robots meta directives


---

## [Configuration](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/getting-started/configuration/) (Getting Started)

---
title: "Configuration"
description: "Every option the plugin accepts, with defaults."
---

Everything lives under a `site` chunk, but per-page overrides go in `pages`.
The plugin fills in defaults for anything you leave out.

## site

| Field           | Type   | Default      | Notes                                                               |
| --------------- | ------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`           | string | required     | Site URL, must be absolute. Used as the canonical base and `og:url` |
| `name`          | string | required     | Site name                                                           |
| `title`         | string | `name`       | Used when a page does not set its own                               |
| `titleTemplate` | string | `%s \| name` | `%s` is replaced with the page title                                |
| `description`   | string | required     | Page description fallback                                           |
| `locale`        | string | `en_US`      | `og:locale`                                                         |
| `author`        | string | -            | `author` meta tag                                                   |
| `image`         | string | -            | Default `og:image`                                                  |
| `twitter`       | object | -            | See [Twitter Cards](../guide/twitter.md)                            |
| `favicon`       | object | -            | See [Favicon & platform icons](../guide/meta-tags.md)               |
| `jsonLd`        | object | -            | See [JSON-LD](../guide/json-ld.md)                                  |

## pages

A map of route to page configurations, of which routes are matched against the built HTML filename.

```ts
pages: {
  "/": { title: "Home" },
  "/about": { title: "About", description: "About us" },
  "/blog/post-slug": { title: "Post", noindex: true },
}
```

### Per-page fields

| Field         | Type             | Notes                                        |
| ------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `title`       | string           | Overrides `site.title`                       |
| `description` | string           | Overrides `site.description`                 |
| `canonical`   | string           | Absolute URL. Defaults to `site.url + route` |
| `noindex`     | boolean          | Adds `noindex`. Excludes from sitemap        |
| `robots`      | string\|string[] | Merged into the robots meta tag              |
| `alternates`  | array            | See [hreflang](../guide/hreflang.md)         |
| `openGraph`   | object           | See [Open Graph](../guide/open-graph.md)     |
| `jsonLd`      | object           | See [JSON-LD](../guide/json-ld.md)           |
| `image`       | string           | Page-specific `og:image`                     |
| `twitter`     | object           | Page-specific Twitter overrides              |

## robots

`robots` can be `false` (skip generation), an array of rules, or a config object.

```ts
robots: {
  userAgent: "*",
  disallow: ["/api", "*.gif$"],
  allow: ["/public"],
  crawlDelay: 5,
  cleanParam: ["sessionid"],
  host: "example.com",
  sitemap: "https://example.com/sitemap.xml",
  disallowNoindex: true,
  groups: [
    { userAgent: "GoogleBot", disallow: ["/private"] },
  ],
}
```

- `merge` (default `true`): preserve existing `public/robots.txt`, append generated rules, drop duplicates
- `disallowNoindex` (default `false`): also emit `Disallow` for pages with `noindex: true`
- `groups`: following the [RFC 9309](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309) agent groups, each with their own `userAgent`, `disallow`, `allow`, `crawlDelay`, `cleanParam`

## sitemap

```ts
sitemap: {
  exclude: ["/admin"],
  maxUrls: 100_000,
  defaultChangefreq: "weekly",
  defaultPriority: 0.8,
  siteUrl: "https://example.com",
}
```

- `maxUrls` (default `50000`): URL cap. Sitemaps split into multiple files past this
- Image, video and news namespaces are emitted automatically when a page has matching `openGraph` data
- `xhtml:link` alternates are emitted for pages with hreflang companions

## validation

| Value     | Behavior               |
| --------- | ---------------------- |
| `"warn"`  | Log issues (default)   |
| `"error"` | Throw, fails the build |
| `false`   | Disable                |

The plugin checks include enums (`changefreq`, `twitter.card`), required fields, absolute URLs, length budgets (title 60, description 50-160, Twitter 70/200), duplicate titles and canonicals, and conflicting `noindex`/`sitemap` settings, all typical stuff.

## Coexistence

If `vite-plugin-sitemap`, `vite-plugin-pwa` or other detected plugins are present, this plugin warns and bails on generating `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` unless you explicitly enable them: `sitemap: true`, `robots: true`.


---

## [Installation](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/getting-started/installation/) (Getting Started)

---
title: "Installation"
description: "Install vite-plugin-seo-meta and set up its peer dependency."
---

Install the plugin (It (obviously) needs Vite as a peer dependency).

```bash
npm i -D vite-plugin-seo-meta vite
```

Vite 5 or newer is required.

The plugin is ESM only. If your project is CommonJS, switch to ESM (easier said than done, to be fair) or use the `.cjs` build.

## Build output

The plugin builds to `dist/index.js` (ESM) and `dist/index.cjs` (CommonJS). The runtime helper is a separate entry (as why would you want to compile a vite-plugin for web, and vice versa):

```ts
import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime";
```

Importing the runtime pulls in the client-side navigation handler. It is tree-shaken (aka, yeeted) out of the main build if you do not use it.


---

## [Quick Start](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/getting-started/quickstart/) (Getting Started)

---
title: "Quick Start"
description: "Add SEO to a Vite app in two minutes."
---

Add the plugin to `vite.config.ts` and give it a `site` block.
Nicely enough, that's the minimum effort you have to do, as everything else gets sensible defaults.
Please _do_ fill out the rest though haha, it's worth it.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { seo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    seo({
      site: {
        url: "https://example.com",
        name: "My Site",
        title: "My Site",
        titleTemplate: "%s | My Site",
        description: "My awesome site",
      },
    }),
  ],
});
```

## Per-page overrides

Put a `seo.config.ts` next to `vite.config.ts` and the plugin loads it automatically, no questions asked.

```ts
import { defineSeoConfig } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta";

export default defineSeoConfig({
  site: {
    url: "https://example.com",
    name: "My Site",
    title: "My Site",
    titleTemplate: "%s | My Site",
    description: "My awesome site",
  },
  pages: {
    "/about": {
      title: "About Us",
      description: "Who we are and what we build.",
    },
    "/blog/hello-world": {
      title: "Hello, world",
      description: "My first post on this site.",
      noindex: true,
    },
  },
});
```

## How the puzzle assembles

- `site` holds the defaults every page inherits
- `pages` overrides specific routes. A page can set any field the site has, plus `noindex`, `canonical`, `alternates` and `robots`
- The plugin merges site defaults with the matching page, then outputs tags at build time


---

## [hreflang](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/hreflang/) (Guide)

---
title: "hreflang"
description: "Tell search engines which language and region variant of a page to show."
---

hreflang alternates are emitted as `<link rel="alternate">` tags. They live in `pages[].alternates`.

```ts
pages: {
  "/": {
    alternates: [
      { hreflang: "en", href: "https://example.com/" },
      { hreflang: "es", href: "https://example.com/es/" },
      { hreflang: "x-default", href: "https://example.com/" },
    ],
  },
}
```

![alt text](./assets/images/hreflang.png)

## What each field means

- `hreflang`: the language or region code. Use [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) for languages, or `en-US`, `es-MX` for language-region pairs. Region codes come from [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) which are the two-letter country codes
- `href`: the **absolute** URL of that variant
- `x-default`: a catch-all for searchers who do not match any listed language or region. Point it at your default page

## Rules

- Every `href` must be an absolute URL
- The page should list itself in its own alternates. If the page is the English variant, include `{ hreflang: "en", href: "https://example.com/" }`
- The plugin emits `xhtml:link` alternates in `sitemap.xml` for pages that have hreflang companions
- hreflang URLs must all resolve to the same host. The sitemap enforces this.

## Big "Don't Do This"

Listing a variant that does not exist. If you say `es` points to `https://example.com/es/` and that page is a 404, search engines will show the error to Spanish users. So, obviously, don't mess up your deployments.

## When to use it

- You have the same content in multiple languages
- You have the same content for different regions (`.com`, `.com.au`, `.ca`)
- You want to tell search engines which variant to show which user

If you do not have multiple languages, leave `alternates` out. The plugin does not add anything on its own (yet? maybe.)


---

## [JSON-LD](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/json-ld/) (Guide)

---
title: "JSON-LD"
description: "Structured data for search engines: Organization, WebSite, Article, Product, BreadcrumbList and ImageObject."
---

JSON-LD, also known as JSON Linked Data, is a way to provide structured data to search engines. It is a standard format for describing the content of a web page for better indexing and results.This plugin emits JSON-LD as `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks. Enable the types you need in `site.jsonLd` and add per-page data in `pages[].jsonLd`.

![example JSON-LD](./assets/images/json-ld.png)

The format is pretty well standardized at [json-ld.org](https://json-ld.org/) and the vocabulary for what you can describe lives at [schema.org](https://schema.org/). The plugin models the common types from schema.org; anything not covered goes through `extra`! If you feel that any type is missing or should be added to the plugin, please open an issue or PR, I'd love to add it!

## Organization

```ts
site: {
  jsonLd: { organization: true },
}
```

This emits an `Organization` block with the site name and URL. Add a logo:

```ts
site: {
  name: "My Site",
  jsonLd: { organization: { logo: "https://example.com/logo.png" } },
}
```

## WebSite

```ts
site: {
  jsonLd: { website: true },
}
```

Emits a `WebSite` block. Set `site.searchAction` to add a search box to the result:

```ts
site: {
  jsonLd: {
    website: {
      searchAction: {
        target: "https://example.com/search?q={query}",
        queryInput: "required name=query",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Article

```ts
pages: {
  "/blog/hello-world": {
    jsonLd: {
      article: {
        headline: "Hello, world",
        type: "BlogPosting",
        author: { name: "Alice" },
        datePublished: "2024-01-15",
        dateModified: "2024-06-20",
        description: "My first post on this site.",
        image: "https://example.com/post.png",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Note: `author` can be a single object or an array. `type` defaults to `Article`; set `BlogPosting`, `NewsArticle` or others as needed.

## Product

```ts
pages: {
  "/products/widget": {
    jsonLd: {
      product: {
        name: "Widget",
        image: "https://example.com/widget.png",
        description: "A widget for doing things.",
        sku: "WIDGET-001",
        brand: "My Brand",
        mpn: "MPN-001",
        offers: {
          price: 19.99,
          priceCurrency: "USD",
          availability: "InStock",
          url: "https://example.com/products/widget",
        },
        review: {
          reviewRating: { ratingValue: 5, bestRating: 5 },
          author: { name: "Bob" },
          reviewBody: "Best widget I have owned.",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## BreadcrumbList

```ts
pages: {
  "/products/widget": {
    jsonLd: {
      breadcrumb: [
        { name: "Home", item: "https://example.com/" },
        { name: "Products", item: "https://example.com/products" },
        { name: "Widget", item: "https://example.com/products/widget" },
      ],
    },
  },
}
```

## ImageObject

```ts
pages: {
  "/gallery/photo-1": {
    jsonLd: {
      image: {
        url: "https://example.com/photo-1.jpg",
        description: "A photo of a thing",
        license: "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/",
        author: { name: "Alice" },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Extra

If the plugin does not cover a type you need, pass raw JSON-LD through `extra`:

```ts
jsonLd: {
  extra: [
    {
      "@type": "HowTo",
      name: "How to do the thing",
      step: [{ "@type": "HowToStep", text: "Do the thing" }],
    },
  ],
}
```

`extra` is emitted verbatim. It is what you would call an "escape hatch" for types the plugin does not model. If you feel that any type is missing or should be added to the plugin, please open an issue or PR.


---

## [Meta Tags](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/meta-tags/) (Guide)

---
title: "Meta Tags"
description: "How the plugin emits title, description, canonical and robots meta tags."
---

The plugin emits standard meta tags (`<meta>` tags) for every page. You set the defaults in `site` and override per page in `pages`.

## title

The `<title>` comes from the page `title`, falling back to `site.title`. The `titleTemplate` wraps it.

You can pass a string or a function to `titleTemplate`. The string should contain `%s` where the page title should go. The function receives the page title and returns a string, for example:

```ts
site: {
  title: "My Site",
  titleTemplate: "%s | My Site",
},
pages: { "/about": { title: "About Us" } },
```

Renders as `<title>About Us | My Site</title>`.

Keep titles under 60 characters. The validator enforces this, and it's generally a good idea to follow it: titles that are too long may be truncated in search results... and that's bad.

## description

The `<meta name="description">` comes from the page `description`, falling back to `site.description`.

```ts
site: { description: "My awesome site" },
pages: { "/about": { description: "Who we are and what we build." } },
```

Keep descriptions between 50 and 160 characters. Also enforced.

## canonical

`<link rel="canonical">` points to the page URL. It defaults to `site.url + route`. Set it explicitly when the same content lives at multiple URLs.

```ts
pages: {
  "/product": { canonical: "https://example.com/products/widget" },
}
```

Canonicals must be absolute URLs. The validator checks this. Google's guidance on canonicals is [available here](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) and it's worth reading if you're ever unsure whether to set one!

## robots meta

**Per-page** `robots` adds a `<meta name="robots">` value. It does not touch `robots.txt`, which is generated separately.

The valid directives are documented in Google's [robots meta tag reference](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag). The plugin accepts all of them!

```ts
pages: { "/private": { robots: "noindex, nofollow" } }
```

`noindex: true` is shorthand for `robots: "noindex"`. It also (obviously)excludes the page from `sitemap.xml`.

## noindex and crawling

A page with `noindex: true` tells crawlers not to index it, but by default it does not add a `Disallow` rule to `robots.txt`. Crawlers can still reach the page to see the `noindex` directive. This is done because some crawlers (like Googlebot) still index pages... even if they're marked `noindex`, cause Google just do be like that sometimes.

To block crawling outright, set `disallowNoindex: true` on the `robots` config:

```ts
robots: {
  disallowNoindex: true;
}
```

## Favicon and platform icons (subject to change)

The `favicon` block emits link tags and meta tags for browsers and platforms:

```ts
site: {
  favicon: {
    icon: "/favicon.ico",
    appleTouchIcon: "/apple-touch-icon.png",
    appleTouchIconPrecomposed: "/apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png",
    manifest: "/manifest.json",
    maskIcon: "/mask-icon.svg",
    maskIconColor: "#000000",
    mobileWebApp: {
      title: "My App",
      capable: true,
      statusBarStyle: "black-translucent",
    },
    msapplication: {
      tileColor: "#ffffff",
      tileImage: "/tile.png",
      config: "/browserconfig.xml",
    },
  },
}
```

- `maskIconColor` defaults to `#000000`
- `mobileWebApp` covers `apple-mobile-web-app-title`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` and `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`
- `msapplication` covers `msapplication-TileColor`, `msapplication-TileImage` and `msapplication-config`

I plan to eventually fold this into the main seo block and automatically fill in the various fields and manifest and browserconfig files from the existing data, and also generate all icons from a single source image. For now, you have to provide all of these manually.


---

## [Open Graph](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/open-graph/) (Guide)

---
title: "Open Graph"
description: "og:* tags for Facebook, LinkedIn and every platform that reads them."
---

Open Graph, also known as `og:*` tags, is a universal standard for describing _how_ a page looks when shared on social media. It's used by Facebook, LinkedIn, Discord, Slack (oh hi Hack Club), and **many** other platforms. Suffice to say, they're important.

The spec exists at [ogp.me](https://ogp.me/).

> Side note: In my opinion, that's how spec pages should be in my opinion, as it's pretty easy to parse, not 20 pages and written in legalese lol.

They are emitted from the `openGraph` block, which inherits from `site` defaults.

## Basic tags

```ts
pages: {
  "/": {
    openGraph: {
      title: "My Site",
      description: "My awesome site",
      type: "website",
      url: "https://example.com",
      image: "https://example.com/og.png",
      siteName: "My Site",
      locale: "en_US",
    },
  },
}
```

- `type` defaults to `website`. Set `article` for blog posts, `book`, `profile`, `music.*`, `video.*` or others... based on what your page is about.
- `url` defaults to the page canonical
- `image` defaults to `site.image`

## Article type

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "article",
  article: {
    publishedTime: "2024-01-15",
    modifiedTime: "2024-06-20",
    author: "https://example.com/authors/alice",
    section: "Technology",
    tag: ["typescript", "vite"],
  },
}
```

`author` can be a single URL or an array. `tag` is the same.

## Book type

<!-- Yeah that's a real book! -->

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "book",
  book: {
    author: "https://example.com/authors/popper",
    isbn: "978-3-16-148410-0",
    releaseDate: "2019-02-01",
    tag: ["fiction"],
  },
}
```

## Profile type

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "profile",
  profile: {
    firstName: "Karl",
    lastName: "Popper",
    username: "karlpopper",
    gender: "male",
  },
}
```

## Music types

`music.album`, `music.playlist` and `music.radio_station` share the same fields:

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "music.album",
  music: {
    duration: 213,
    musician: ["https://example.com/artists/queen"],
    song: [{ url: "https://example.com/songs/we-will-rock-you", disc: 1, track: 1 }],
    releaseDate: "1977-10-21",
  },
}
```

`song` and `album` are arrays of `{ url, disc?, track? }`. `disc` and `track` default to 1.

## Video types

`video.movie`, `video.episode` and `video.series`:

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "video.movie",
  video: {
    actor: [{ url: "https://example.com/people/tom-hanks", role: "Forrest Gump" }],
    director: ["https://example.com/people/robert-zemeckis"],
    duration: 142 * 60 + 24,
    releaseDate: "1994-06-23",
    series: "https://example.com/series/futurama",
  },
}
```

## Structured images, audio and video

Instead of a single `image` URL, pass structured entries with extra properties:

```ts
openGraph: {
  images: [
    { url: "https://example.com/og-1200x630.png", width: 1200, height: 630, alt: "Share this page" },
  ],
  audios: [{ url: "https://example.com/podcast.mp3" }],
  videos: [{ url: "https://example.com/trailer.mp4" }],
}
```

Structured images override the flat `image` field when present.

## payment.link

```ts
openGraph: {
  type: "payment.link",
  payment: {
    description: "One month subscription",
    currency: "USD",
    amount: 9.99,
    status: "PENDING",
    id: "sub_123",
    successUrl: "https://example.com/thanks",
  },
}
```

## determiner

```ts
openGraph: {
  determiner: "auto";
}
```

Valid values: `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"noun"`. A determiner is the word that comes before the title (noun), like "a," "an," or "the." By default, it's set to auto, which means the system decides whether or not to include it.


---

## [robots.txt](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/robots/) (Guide)

---
title: "robots.txt"
description: "Generate robots.txt following RFC 9309 with agent groups, wildcards and crawl delays."
---

[RFC 9309](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309.html) defines the robots.txt standard. Originally made by Martijn Koster in 1994 [(the original spec)](https://www.robotstxt.org/orig.html), because robots kept crawling sites and causing a ruckus. (Seems mighty familiar to today's AI bots, doesn't it?) The standard has been (barely) updated over the years, and this plugin implements the latest version.

![image of RFC 9309](./assets/images/Tracer_mvn05nlb.png)

It's generated at build time. It can be disabled, replaced, or merged with an existing file.

## Basic rules

```ts
robots: {
  userAgent: "*",
  disallow: ["/api", "*.gif$"],
  allow: ["/public"],
  crawlDelay: 5,
  cleanParam: ["sessionid"],
  host: "example.com",
  sitemap: "https://example.com/sitemap.xml",
  disallowNoindex: true,
}
```

- `userAgent`: who the rules apply to. Default `*`
- `disallow`: paths to block. Supports `*` (match anything) and `$` (end of string)
- `allow`: paths to explicitly permit, overriding `disallow`
- `crawlDelay`: delay in seconds
- `cleanParam`: URL parameters to ignore when crawling
- `host`: the `Host:` record
- `sitemap`: URL to advertise, or `false` to omit. Defaults to `site.url + /sitemap.xml`
- `disallowNoindex`: also block pages with `noindex: true`

## Wildcards

`*` matches any sequence of characters. `$` matches the end of the URL.

```ts
disallow: ["/api", "*.gif$", "/private/*"];
```

- `/api` blocks `/api`, `/api/foo`, `/api/foo/bar` (basically anything under it)
- `*.gif$` blocks `/img/cat.gif` but not `/img/cat.png` (which... is obviously not a GIF)
- `/private/*` blocks everything under `/private` (also `/private/foo`, `/private/foo/bar`, etc.) but not `/private` itself. Use `/private` to block that too.

`allow` takes priority when a path matches both. So `allow: ["/public"]` lets crawlers through even if `disallow: ["/"]`.

## Agent groups

Different crawlers get different rules:

```ts
robots: {
  groups: [
    {
      userAgent: "GoogleBot",
      disallow: ["/private"],
      crawlDelay: 2,
    },
    {
      userAgent: "BingBot",
      allow: ["/"],
    },
  ],
}
```

Each group has its own `userAgent`, `disallow`, `allow`, `crawlDelay` and `cleanParam`. The default group (top-level fields) applies to `*`.

## Merge with an existing file

By default the plugin preserves `robots.txt` in the output directory and appends generated rules. Duplicates are dropped.

To overwrite instead, set `merge: false`:

```ts
robots: {
  merge: false;
}
```

## noindex and crawling

A page with `noindex: true` tells crawlers not to index it. By default it does not add a `Disallow` rule, so crawlers can still reach the page to see the directive.

To block crawling outright:

```ts
robots: {
  disallowNoindex: true;
}
```

## Raw lines

Append literal lines after the generated rules:

```ts
robots: {
  rules: [
    "User-agent: *",
    "Disallow: /",
  ],
}
```

Use this when the plugin does not cover something. The lines are emitted verbatim.


---

## [sitemap.xml](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/sitemap/) (Guide)

---
title: "sitemap.xml"
description: "Generate sitemap.xml with image, video and news namespaces, plus URL caps."
---

A sitemap is an XML file that lists all the pages on your site. It's extremely useful for search engines, as it's a easily parsible list of all your pages. It can also include images, videos and news articles.

The protocol is documented at [sitemaps.org](https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html). I tried to follow this as closely as possible, but if you notice any discrepancies, please open an issue or PR!!!

![alt text](./assets/images/Tracer_mvmzfk8e.png)

`sitemap.xml` is generated at build time from the `pages` map. It lists every route that is not `noindex` and not in `exclude`.

## Basic options

```ts
sitemap: {
  exclude: ["/admin", "/login"],
  maxUrls: 100_000,
  defaultChangefreq: "weekly",
  defaultPriority: 0.8,
  siteUrl: "https://example.com",
}
```

- `exclude`: routes to leave out
- `maxUrls`: URLs per sitemap file. Default `50000`
- `defaultChangefreq`: fallback for pages without one
- `defaultPriority`: fallback for pages without one
- `siteUrl`: origin used to enforce a single-host sitemap

## changefreq

Per-page or global and valid values: `always`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly`, `never`.

```ts
pages: {
  "/blog/hello-world": { changefreq: "weekly", priority: 0.9 },
  "/": { changefreq: "daily", priority: 1.0 },
}
```

## maxUrls and splitting

Past `maxUrls` URLs, the plugin splits into multiple files: `sitemap.xml`, `sitemap-1.xml`, `sitemap-2.xml`, and so on. The index file lists them all and is the only one that you provide to Google Search Console or other search engine tools.

The default of 50000 is the [sitemaps.org](https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html) recommendation. Most sites should never hit it. Raise it if you have a large site and want fewer files!

## Image namespace

When a page has `openGraph.image` (or structured `images`), the sitemap entry gets `<image:image>`:

```xml
<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/blog/hello-world</loc>
  <lastmod>2024-06-20</lastmod>
  <changefreq>weekly</changefreq>
  <priority>0.9</priority>
  <image:image>
    <image:loc>https://example.com/post.png</image:loc>
    <image:title>Hello, world</image:title>
    <image:caption>My first post on this site.</image:caption>
  </image:image>
</url>
```

`image:title` comes from the page title. `image:caption` from the page description

## Video namespace

When a page has `openGraph.video`, the sitemap entry gets `<video:video>`:

```xml
<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/watch/trailer</loc>
  <video:video>
    <video:thumbnail_loc>https://example.com/thumb.png</video:thumbnail_loc>
    <video:title>Trailer</video:title>
    <video:description>Watch the trailer.</video:description>
    <video:content_loc>https://example.com/trailer.mp4</video:content_loc>
    <video:duration>142</video:duration>
  </video:video>
</url>
```

A `thumbnail` is required for video entries! Pages without one are **automatically** skipped rather than emitting invalid XML.

## News namespace

When a page sets `openGraph.article.publishedTime`, the sitemap entry gets a `<news:news>` block:

```xml
<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/blog/breaking</loc>
  <news:news>
    <news:publication>
      <news:name>My Site</news:name>
      <news:language>en</news:language>
    </news:publication>
    <news:publication_date>2024-06-20</news:publication_date>
    <news:title>Breaking</news:title>
  </news:news>
</url>
```

## xhtml:link alternates

Pages with hreflang alternates get `<xhtml:link>` entries in their sitemap URL:

```xml
<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/</loc>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/"/>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="es" href="https://example.com/es/"/>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/"/>
</url>
```

## Single-host enforcement

All sitemap URLs must share the same host as `site.url`. If a page canonical points elsewhere, the entry is skipped. This keeps the sitemap valid. Open an issue/PR if you want to allow cross-host sitemaps.


---

## [SPA Runtime](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/spa-runtime/) (Guide)

---
title: "SPA Runtime"
description: "Update SEO tags when the URL changes in a single-page app."
---

SPA apps have a problem. If you navigate to a new route, the `<title>` and `<meta>` tags do not update. This is because the plugin only injects them at build time.So, the plugin injects tags at build time for the initial HTML. When the client navigates to a new route, the tags do not update on their own so you need to call `applySeo()`.

```ts
import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime";

function onRouteChange() {
  applySeo({ title: "New Page", description: "..." });
}
```

## How it works

`applySeo(page, site?)` merges the page data with the injected site config. Pass `site` explicitly when you need a different site than the one the plugin injected. Omit it and the plugin uses the config from the build.

It only updates head elements the plugin manages and your own tags are left alone once the page is loaded!

## What it updates

- `<title>`
- `<meta name="description">`
- `<meta name="robots">`
- `<link rel="canonical">`
- Open Graph tags
- Twitter Card tags
- JSON-LD scripts

## When to call it

Call it after every route change. In a router, that is the navigation callback:

```ts
// vue-router
router.afterEach((to) => {
  applySeo({ title: to.meta.title, description: to.meta.description });
});

// react-router
useEffect(() => {
  applySeo({ title: location.pathname, description: "..." });
}, [location]);
```

## What it does not do

`applySeo` updates tags. It does not push history, change the URL, or update the browser title bar. Your router handles that! Don't just rely on `applySeo` if you're making an SPA (if that wasn't obvious already)!

It also does not fetch data, as you should already have it available. Pass the metadata you already have!


---

## [Twitter Cards](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/twitter/) (Guide)

---
title: "Twitter Cards"
description: "How the plugin emits twitter:* tags for summary, player and app cards."
---

Twitter Cards control how a link looks on Twitter (i'm not calling it X). They live in the `twitter` block, which inherits from `site.twitter`.

```ts
site: {
  twitter: {
    site: "@Twitter",
    creator: "@Twitter",
  },
}
```

![example ](./assets/images/image.png)

> Side note: X decided to delete all their documentation, so I had to find them in the [Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org/web/20221010220601/https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/abouts-cards), which was tedium.

## Card types

| Value                 | Use case                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `summary`             | Small card with thumbnail      |
| `summary_large_image` | Large image card               |
| `player`              | Embedded video or audio player |
| `app`                 | Promote an app                 |

## Basic fields

```ts
twitter: {
  card: "summary_large_image",
  site: "@mysite",
  creator: "@alice",
  title: "Hello, world",
  description: "My first post on this site.",
  image: "https://example.com/card.png",
  imageAlt: "A screenshot of the post",
  imageWidth: 1200,
  imageHeight: 630,
}
```

- `site` and `creator` are `@handles`
- `imageAlt` is required when `image` is set. Max 420 characters
- `imageWidth` and `imageHeight` are the card image dimensions in pixels

## Numeric IDs

Instead of `@handles`, use numeric IDs:

```ts
twitter: {
  siteId: "1234567890",
  creatorId: "0987654321",
}
```

`siteId` replaces `site`. `creatorId` replaces `creator`. Use whichever you have.

## Label and data pairs

Summary cards can carry two label/value pairs:

```ts
twitter: {
  card: "summary",
  label1: "Price",
  data1: "$199",
  label2: "Stock",
  data2: "In stock",
}
```

## Player Card

For embedded video or audio:

```ts
twitter: {
  card: "player",
  player: {
    url: "https://example.com/player.html",
    width: 1280,
    height: 720,
    stream: "https://example.com/stream.mp4",
  },
}
```

- `url` is the HTTPS iframe URL.
- `width` and `height` are the iframe dimensions in pixels.
- `stream` is optional. It points to a raw video or audio stream.

## App Card

Promote an app. One entry per platform:

```ts
twitter: {
  card: "app",
  apps: {
    iphone: { name: "My App", id: "1234567890", url: "myapp://open" },
    ipad: { name: "My App", id: "1234567890", url: "myapp://open" },
    googleplay: { name: "My App", id: "com.example.myapp", url: "myapp://open" },
  },
  country: "US",
}
```

- `name` is the app name (who knew)
- `id` is the app store ID
- `url` is a custom URL scheme. It must include `://`. You also have to register the scheme in your app. See [Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/defining-a-custom-url-scheme-for-your-app) and [Google](https://developer.android.com/training/app-links/deep-linking) for details.
- `country` is the two-letter ISO country code for the App Store that holds the app.


---

## [Validation](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/guide/validation/) (Guide)

---
title: "Validation"
description: "Catch misconfigured SEO before it ships."
---

The plugin validates config at build time. By default it logs issues and continues. Set `validate: "error"` to fail the build. I'd recommend doing this in CI, so you catch problems before they reach production!!!

```ts
seo({ validate: "error" });
```

## Modes

| Value     | Behavior               |
| --------- | ---------------------- |
| `"warn"`  | Log issues (default)   |
| `"error"` | Throw, fails the build |
| `false`   | Disable                |

## What it checks

### Enums

- `changefreq` must be one of `always`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly`, `never`
- `twitter.card` must be one of `summary`, `summary_large_image`, `player`, `app`

### Required fields

- `site.url` must be set
- `site.name` and `site.description` are required when their page-level values are missing

### Absolute URLs

Canonicals, `og:url`, `twitter:image` and `twitter:player` URLs **must be absolute**. Relative URLs are resolved against `site.url` before validation, so this check runs on the resolved value.

### Length budgets

| Field                 | Limit             |
| --------------------- | ----------------- |
| `title`               | 60 characters     |
| `description`         | 50-160 characters |
| `twitter:title`       | 70 characters     |
| `twitter:description` | 200 characters    |
| `twitter:image:alt`   | 420 characters    |

### Duplicates

- Two pages with the same `title`
- Two pages with the same `canonical`

### Conflicts

- A page with `noindex: true` that is also in `sitemap.xml` (noindex pages are excluded from the sitemap by default, but this catches explicit overrides, juuuust in case)
- A page with `sitemap: false` that still has hreflang alternates

## How to fix

The validator reports the field, the route, and the problem. Fix the field and rebuild. It does not guess what you meant... because well... it shouldn't; the SEO checks here are strict. If you want to disable a check, set `validate: false` or remove the field entirely.


---

## [vite-plugin-seo-meta](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/)

---
title: "vite-plugin-seo-meta"
description: "All-in-one Vite plugin that generates meta tags, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter Cards, JSON-LD, hreflang, robots.txt and sitemap.xml for your app."
---

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

::: hero layout:split glow:true

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD025 -->
# vite-plugin-seo-meta

Serverless SEO for Vite. One plugin generates `<title>`, meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, Twitter Cards, JSON-LD, hreflang, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. Zero-config defaults, per-page overrides. Works for SPA, MPA, SSG and prerendered builds.

::: tag "Vite"
::: tag "SEO"
::: tag "TypeScript"

::: button "Quick Start" ./getting-started/quickstart.md icon:play
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD034 -->
::: button "Live Demo" external:https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/demo/ icon:monitor
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD034 -->
::: button "GitHub" external:https://github.com/NellowTCS/vite-plugin-seo-meta icon:github

== side

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { seo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    seo({
      site: {
        url: "https://example.com",
        name: "My Site",
        title: "My Site",
        titleTemplate: "%s | My Site",
        description: "My awesome site",
      },
    }),
  ],
});
```

::: /hero

<!-- prettier-ignore-end -->

## Why this plugin

Writing SEO by hand means repeating the same tags for every page, keeping them in sync when the site changes, and forgetting a field on the one page you forget at 3 AM, or deleting mysterious ones that keep your site up top on Google. So... this plugin generates them from a single config and per-page overrides, so the tags are always consistent.

It also handles the files that are très important:

- `robots.txt` follows [RFC 9309](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309) and happens to support agent groups, `Allow`/`Disallow` wildcards and `Crawl-delay`
- `sitemap.xml` supports image, video and news namespaces with single-host enforcement and a URL capacity (extensible)
- Twitter Cards have the typical summary, player and app cards with `:site:id` and `:creator:id` variants
- Favicon and platform icons cover `apple-touch-icon`, `mask-icon`, mobile web app and `msapplication` tags

## What it does not do

This plugin does not generate social images or app icons (very **big** _Yet_). That is a future thing I plan to add hehe.

## Get started

- [Installation](./getting-started/installation.md)
- [Quick Start](./getting-started/quickstart.md)
- [Configuration](./getting-started/configuration.md)

## [Config Reference](https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/reference/config/) (Reference)

## `SeoPluginOptions`

```ts
{
  site?: SiteConfig;
  pages?: Record<string, PageMeta>;
  robots?: "auto" | boolean | RobotsFileOptions;
  sitemap?: "auto" | boolean | SitemapOptions;
  validate?: "warn" | "error" | false;
  configFile?: string | false;
}
```

## `SiteConfig`

```ts
{
  url: string;
  name?: string;
  title?: string;
  titleTemplate?: string;
  description?: string;
  image?: string;
  imageAlt?: string;
  twitter?: string | TwitterInfo;
  locale?: string;
  lang?: string;
  author?: string;
  keywords?: string | string[];
  robotsByUserAgent?: Record<string, string | RobotsDirectives>;
  favicon?: FaviconConfig;
  openGraph?: OpenGraphInfo;
  jsonLd?: JsonLdConfig;
}
```

`twitter` accepts a bare `@handle` as shorthand for `twitter:site`.

## `PageMeta`

```ts
{
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  canonical?: string;
  lang?: string;
  image?: string;
  imageAlt?: string;
  keywords?: string | string[];
  author?: string;
  noindex?: boolean;
  robots?: string | RobotsDirectives;
  robotsByUserAgent?: Record<string, string | RobotsDirectives>;
  openGraph?: OpenGraphInfo;
  twitter?: TwitterInfo;
  jsonLd?: JsonLdConfig;
  alternates?: HreflangAlternate[];
  sitemap?: boolean;
  priority?: number;
  changefreq?: SitemapChangefreq;
  lastmod?: string | Date;
  meta?: Record<string, string>;
  links?: Array<{ rel: string; href: string } & Record<string, string>>;
}
```

## `FaviconConfig`

```ts
{
  icon?: string;
  appleTouchIcon?: string;
  appleTouchIconPrecomposed?: string;
  manifest?: string;
  maskIcon?: string;
  maskIconColor?: string;
  themeColor?: string | ThemeColorEntry[];
  mobileWebApp?: MobileWebAppConfig;
  msapplication?: MsTileConfig;
}
```

## `MobileWebAppConfig`

```ts
{

}
```

## `MsTileConfig`

```ts
{
  tileColor?: string;
  tileImage?: string;
  config?: string;
}
```

## `RobotsFileOptions`

```ts
{
  userAgent?: string | string[];
  disallow?: string[];
  allow?: string[];
  groups?: RobotsGroup[];
  rules?: string[];
  sitemap?: string | false;
  merge?: boolean;
  disallowNoindex?: boolean;
  host?: string;
  crawlDelay?: number;
  cleanParam?: string | string[];
}
```

## `RobotsGroup`

```ts
{
  userAgent: string | string[];
  disallow?: string[];
  allow?: string[];
  crawlDelay?: number;
  cleanParam?: string | string[];
}
```

## `SitemapOptions`

```ts
{
  filename?: string;
  exclude?: string[];
  defaultChangefreq?: SitemapChangefreq;
  defaultPriority?: number;
  siteUrl?: string;
  maxUrls?: number;
}
```

## `SitemapChangefreq`

`"always"` | `"hourly"` | `"daily"` | `"weekly"` | `"monthly"` | `"yearly"` | `"never"`

## `ImageRef` / `ImageInput`

```ts
// ImageRef
{
  src: string;
  alt?: string;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  type?: string;
  secureUrl?: string;
  thumbnail?: string;
}

// ImageInput: string | ImageRef | { src?, url?, href?, alt?, width?, height?, type?, secureUrl?, secure_url?, thumbnail? }
```

`thumbnail` is the video sitemap thumbnail URL. Required for video entries.

## `TwitterInfo`

```ts
{
  card?: TwitterCardType;

  description?: string;
  site?: TwitterHandle;
  siteId?: string;

  creatorId?: string;
  image?: string;
  imageAlt?: string;
  imageWidth?: number;
  imageHeight?: number;
  label1?: string;
  data1?: string;
  label2?: string;
  data2?: string;

  apps?: TwitterApps;
}
```

```ts
{
  url: string;

}
```

```ts
  ipad?: TwitterAppEntry;
  googleplay?: TwitterAppEntry;
  country?: string;
}
```

```ts
{
  name?: string;
  id?: string;

}
```

`"summary"` | `"summary_large_image"` | `"player"` | `"app"`

## `JsonLdConfig`

```ts
{
  organization?: boolean | OrganizationJsonLd;
```

## `RobotsDirectives`

```ts
{
  noindex?: boolean;
  nofollow?: boolean;
  none?: boolean;
  all?: boolean;
  nosnippet?: boolean;
  noarchive?: boolean;
  noimageindex?: boolean;
  notranslate?: boolean;
  indexifembedded?: boolean;
  nositelinkssearchbox?: boolean;
  maxSnippet?: number;
  maxImagePreview?: "none" | "standard" | "large";
  maxVideoPreview?: number;
  unavailableAfter?: string | Date;
}
```


---
